_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS R1240's CONTRACT IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- \
crates/mnemosyne-cli/sweeps/fresh-run-cleaning.sweep.json
WHAT THE CONTRACT IS. `--fresh` is what `scripts/verify.sh` does when nobody
says otherwise: for every crate git reports changed against HEAD it runs
`cargo clean -p <crate>`, so no artifact of the code under test can survive
into the run that judges it. That is the second half of the R743 repair — the
lock stops two cargos racing, this stops a stale binary from a race that
already happened — and until R1240 no test reached the branch at all,
because every case in the file passes `--no-fresh`.
SO THE THREE INJECTIONS ARE THE THREE WAYS A FRESH RUN STOPS BEING ONE, and
each is silent in the direction that reads as a working run. The clean is
announced and not run; the population it works from is empty, so the run says
there was nothing to clean; the header stops recording what was cleaned, which
is the only place the answer is kept after the run. None of them is red
anywhere else, and none of them prints an error.
RUN IT LOCALLY. The harness edits this tree and writes the firing record
beside this file, so a run sent to a build machine leaves its evidence on a
throwaway copy (R1205's carry, and the `writes` line in the declaration).

injections.name: the-clean-is-announced-and-not-run
injections.why: the announcement and the clean are two lines, and only one of them is what a reader sees. A run that prints `fresh: cargo clean -p x` and cleans nothing is indistinguishable from a working one — and what it leaves behind is exactly the stale artifact this script was written after: a deterministic regression that reads as a flake

injections.name: the-population-of-changed-crates-is-never-asked-for
injections.why: the quiet direction of the whole branch. With nothing to iterate the run reports `no uncommitted crate changes; nothing to clean` and carries on — a true-sounding sentence about a tree that has them — so a fresh run becomes a `--no-fresh` run everywhere at once, and the only sign is that a rebuild did not happen

edits.from:
changed_crates="$(git diff --name-only HEAD -- crates/ 2>/dev/null \
    | sed -n 's#^crates/\([^/]*\)/.*#\1#p' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')"

injections.name: the-header-forgets-what-a-fresh-run-cleaned
injections.why: the record rather than the act, and it is the reason the question is asked before the log is opened. The header is the only place a run's answer to `which crates were cleaned` survives, and a log that has stopped carrying it looks complete: the run is green, the cleaning happened, and a later reader diagnosing a rebuild has nothing to read
